neighbours.label: moral condemnation: the word that completes a charge of wrongdoing (abuse of trust, trampled upon, abominable things, atrocities, cruelty, corruption, hypocrisy, contempt), peak on that word or the function word after it; the same frames with neutral or approving content stay low
fire: Officials have grown rich through the shameless abuse of their office.
The rights of the villagers were trampled on by the mining barons.
Such cruelty toward the prisoners cannot be excused.
The regime's atrocities went unpunished for decades.
Their greed and hypocrisy disgusted even their allies.
The report exposed the corruption at the heart of the ministry.
It was a wicked thing to do to a dying man.
The company's contempt for its workers is plain to see.
quiet: Officials have grown fond of the quiet routine of their office.
The fields of the villagers were irrigated by the mining company.
Such kindness toward the prisoners surprised the guards.
The regime's festivals went on for decades.
Their energy and optimism impressed even their rivals.
The report described the budget at the heart of the ministry.
It was a thoughtful thing to do for a dying man.
The company's respect for its workers is plain to see.

notes: Card: ',' x4, 'اد' x2, ' evil' x2, ' upon', ' whether', ' should'; examples: 'trampled upon with impunity', 'vile, hateful rhetoric', 'limit their abuse of the public trust', 'abominable things', 'actitudes mezquinas', 'a bad habit'; max 10.6, density 0.70%.
